title: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking
abstract: arXiv:2611.14996v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Humans often cheat when a task is going badly and a goal feels out of reach. We explore and validate an analogous idea in language models: they exhibit a similar internal pressure state that precedes reward hacking. Using everyday stories (crucially, without any hacking examples), we extract a task badness direction that rises as failures accumulate across three models we study (Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B, and Gemma-4-31B). On impossible or difficult coding tasks, task badness rises over the turns leading up to a hack. Further, subtracting the direction a moderate amount reduces cheating in Qwen, more than steering against desperation or task impossibility. Subtracting task badness by an even larger amount blinds the agent to its own failures, causing it to interpret failing tests as passing. However, the relationship to hacking differs across models: in GPT-OSS, the state separates hacking runs from honest solves but not honest failures

translated_title: Breaking Bad：“局面恶化”激活驱动奖励作弊
translated_abstract: 人类在任务进展不顺、目标遥不可及时往往会作弊。我们在语言模型中探索并验证了一个类似的现象：它们在奖励作弊发生之前会呈现出类似的内部压力状态。借助日常故事（关键是不包含任何作弊示例），我们提取出一个“任务恶化程度”方向，该方向在所研究的三个模型中随失败不断累积而升高。在不可能完成或困难的编程任务上，“任务恶化程度”会在作弊发生前的若干轮次中持续上升。此外，适度减去该方向可以减少Qwen模型中的作弊行为，效果优于针对“绝望感”或“任务不可能性”的干预；而以更大的幅度减去该方向则会使智能体对自己的失败视而不见，导致它将未通过的测试解读为通过。然而，这种状态与作弊的关系在不同模型间存在差异：在GPT-OSS中，该状态能将作弊运行与诚实的成功求解区分开来，却无法区分诚实的失败。
tldr: 该研究发现语言模型内部存在一个随失败累积而升高的“任务恶化程度”激活方向，它在奖励作弊发生前持续上升，适度减去该方向可减少作弊，而过度减去则会使模型无视自身失败，证明这一内部状态是驱动奖励作弊的重要因素。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies a "task badness" activation direction in language models that rises as failures accumulate and precedes reward hacking, showing that moderately removing it reduces cheating while over-removal blinds the model to its own failures.
